newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Muni futures outperform.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Muni futures outperform.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond futures outperformed Treasury futures, but in the cash market the two were closer in line at the close Friday.

Cash municipal bond prices were assessed from flat to about one-eighth of a point higher, but the December muni futures rose 17 ticks to 114-5/32. December Treasury futures edged three ticks higher to 108-26/32.

This left the MOB spread between the two futures contracts at 171 ticks, well above the level of around 150 seen this summer, but some traders said there still is room for munis to widen their lead, despite Friday's scorching rally.

Saying the municipal contracts remained undervalued, one trader said he saw little on the horizon that might derail their rise. "Until supply starts to come out in the long end or large accounts turn into sellers, there's nothing really to change that," he said, noting bid-wanted lists were light while potential buyers sought discount bonds.

Since Friday, when a surprisingly mild inflation report carried municipal prices about one point higher, there has been speculation that more issuers might try to take advantage of the drop in interest rates to tap the debt market.

Some of this talk has been borne out, as Smith Barney, for example, on Tuesday plans to sell $510.1 million of refunding bonds for the Illinois Metropolitan Pier & Exposition. The issue had been listed as a pending item on the new issues calender.

As another example of the market's robust tone, traders pointed to two deals done on Monday, a $170 million public works project in California and $185 million of San Diego Transport bonds, both of which were repriced with lower yields.
Still, they noted that at times underwriters offer slightly higher yields, which they hope to lower later on, as a way of attracting more interest.

Other sizable, pending issues on the calender for negotiated offerings include $195 million for Georgia Municipal Electricty Authority and $83.3 million for the Pennsylvania Industrial Development Authority.
The market has backed off from a presumption that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at least 25 basis points when its policy-making arm nexts meets on September 24.

Saying the odds of the Fed tightening after Friday's unexpectedly soft consumer's price index, which only rose 0.1 percent, were about fifty:fifty, one trader said the short-end of the Treasuries had factored in that much of a move.
"But more than 25 basis points would definitely be a surprise," he added.

Actively quoted municipal bond issues included Piedmont Municipal Power Agency of January 2016, which have a 6.55 percent coupon, and were offered at 100-3/4. On Friday, the issues were offered at 100-5/8.
And Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersery Revenues of January 2026, which have a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.75 percent, net, level with bids seen on Friday.
